extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, patent examiners, patent practitioners, stakeholders, and policymakers (Congress)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and recommendations from the Patent Public Advisory Committee (PPAC) FY2016 Annual Report on evaluating and improving USPTO patent quality, IT, finance, PTAB, pendency, fee policy, and human capital. Targets USPTO internal processes and external stakeholder impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent quality as primary objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizing that the issuance of high quality patents with a reasonable pendency is of critical importance to the economic strength of the United States; patent quality was established as the major focus of the Director's tenure and the USPTO implemented numerous enhanced patent quality initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiatives include applicant participation programs, Master Review Form (MRF), quality review tool to gather uniform review data, delivery of reference material to examiners to ensure consistent decisions, programs to improve clarity of the record, Post Prosecution Pilot (P3), Post Grant Outcomes Pilot, and regular memos/guidelines on 35 U.S.C. § 101. The USPTO solicits comments via the World Class Patent Quality mailbox (worldclasspatentquality@uspto.gov).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisory review and robust feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on supervisory review and a robust feedback system to channel quality comments and suggestions to the examiners, combined with identification of individual or group deficiencies to be addressed with additional training and follow up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervisory Patent Examiners (SPEs) are well positioned to conduct reviews and deliver feedback but must be allowed adequate time to perform these functions and emphasize that this is their primary and most important function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete searches per MPEP covering invention and inventive concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on complete searches as set forth in the Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) covering an invention, as described and claimed, including the inventive concepts toward which the claims appear to be directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searches should locate prior art that would have been found for the claims as originally presented; efforts recommended to reduce final rejections that rely on art that should have been found earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and comprehensive office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Office actions should be clear and comprehensive, identifying how the claim is being interpreted and the passages of the reference(s) being relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear identification of claim interpretation and specific reference passages aids applicants and improves prosecution efficiency and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough treatment of arguments and evidence in responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Thorough treatment of arguments and evidence submitted in response to rejections is required to ensure proper consideration and high-quality outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner work product should fully address applicant-submitted arguments and evidence so that issues are resolved without unnecessary appeals or RCEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mine pre-appeal and appeal conference data to identify patterns/errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate and mine data obtained from pre-appeal brief conferences and appeal conferences to identify patterns or errors and develop steps for quality improvements of final rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These programs weed out improper rejections but are costly; reducing improper finals by analyzing conference data is a worthwhile undertaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce final rejections citing new prior art after small claim changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate and try to reduce the number of final rejections which cite new prior art, particularly following small changes to the claims which should have been recognized as the invention was searched according to MPEP guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some new prior art applied in final rejections should have been located and applied to the claims as originally presented; reducing such instances improves efficiency and reduces applicant/USPTO costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsider compact prosecution / allow additional amendments post-final
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the compact prosecution model to determine if it provides an efficient, effective process; consider allowing other options such as an additional amendment after a final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approximately 30% of filed applications are Requests for Continued Examination (RCEs) suggesting single round prosecution may be insufficient; reconsideration could reduce RCEs and long-term USPTO workload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency across examiners and predictability of outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on improving the consistency of rejections and quality of actions from the Patent Examining Corps so that outcomes are not heavily dependent on which examiner is assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some differences are expected, but more predictable examinations should exist across technologies and especially in 35 U.S.C. § 101 application. Consistency requires supervisory oversight, interventions, and error correction without costly appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide applicants additional prosecution options
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer additional applicant options during prosecution to improve efficiency and reduce costly appeals or RCEs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable initiatives: Post Prosecution Pilot (P3), Post Grant Outcomes Pilot, Clarity of the Record Pilot, Case Studies Pilot, MRF, and stakeholder training and memos providing examples/guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a Master Review Form (MRF) in work-product reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement a Master Review Form for use in all reviews of the work product to gather uniform review data on correctness and clarity into a single database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MRF intended to standardize evaluations and improve the ability to measure and compare quality across examiners and units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of the Record pilot
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot aimed at improving the clarity of the record in prosecution and examiner actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Better record clarity helps applicants, examiners, and downstream adjudicators (e.g., PTAB, courts) understand the rationale for decisions, reducing disputes and uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-Prosecution Pilot (P3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot where applicants may present arguments after a final rejection to a panel of three examiners and receive detailed information regarding the outcome of their evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P3 offers an alternative to RCEs or appeals by providing substantive post-final review; intended to reduce unnecessary RCE filings and improve prosecution efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post Grant Outcomes Pilot
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information from Inter Partes Review (IPR) of patents to the examiner of a pending related application to inform prosecution decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using post-grant proceeding outcomes can improve initial examination quality by leveraging IPR results and avoid issuing patents with defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality measurement and adjusted metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust the metrics utilized to track and report evaluations done by the USPTO of their work product and implement tools to gather uniform review data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality measurement includes new tools, Master Review Form, external quality surveys, pre-appeal/appeal statistics, and a Quality Chats initiative; feedback solicited via WCPQ mailbox.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and stakeholder education
rubrics_metrics.description: Ongoing guidance and training for examiners and stakeholder training on examination practice and procedures to improve consistency and quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training programs include internal examiner training pilots, stakeholder training sessions, regularly distributed memos, guidelines, and examples related to claim examination and case law (e.g., § 101 guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Technology modernization (PE2E, DAV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace antiquated technology and provide new systems (Patents End-to-End, DAV, advanced search tools, official correspondence tool) to improve examiner capabilities and workflow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DAV replaced eDAN providing integrated case management and automation (claim trees, text searching); new search and authoring tools planned; modernization essential to improve examination quality and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systems to support international work sharing and Global Dossier
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement IT systems (e.g., Global Dossier, CPC support) to enable access to contents of applications from other offices and perform searches across multiple offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems enable examiners to include EPO, JPO, KIPO, SIPO art in searches and support work sharing efforts with IP5 offices and other programs like Patent Prosecution Highway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust contingency planning and infrastructure resilience
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure contingency planning and upgrade hardware and backup systems to prevent catastrophic service interruptions like the December 2015 power outage that damaged key IT systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-planning helped but the outage demonstrated unacceptable vulnerabilities; modernization and robust contingency are essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain access to collected fees and adequate operating reserve
rubrics_metrics.description: Continued access by the USPTO to all collected fees and maintenance of the Patent Operating Reserve are crucial for efforts to improve patent quality and replace mission-critical systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY2015/FY2016 spending exceeded collections and used the reserve; sustaining long-term funding is essential for IT, training, and PTAB resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent, periodic fee review and stakeholder input
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the biennial fee review and rulemaking process with public notice and comment and PPAC input to set fees; provide transparency around prioritization of expenditures and use of fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPAC solicited public input and held hearings; suggested publishing more transparency to justify fee increases and how funds are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid punitive RCE fee increases; reduce need for RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconsider proposed increases to RCE fees because applicants often file RCEs out of necessity given examination inefficiencies; higher fees may be an unfair penalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPAC urges focusing on initiatives to reduce the need for RCEs (process changes, training, supervisory review) rather than relying on fee disincentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair excess claim fees and refund mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Reevaluate excess claim fees relative to incremental work; consider refunding excess claim fees when excess claims are canceled in response to a restriction requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees should reflect claims actually examined, not just filed; assessing fees prior to restriction practice can unfairly charge applicants for claims they will not be examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS fee policy that does not discourage timely disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns about proposed IDS fee increases and eliminating 37 C.F.R. 1.97(e) certification; recommend smaller IDS increases and maintaining certification to deter intentional delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High post-first-action IDS fees could deter prompt disclosure of new prior art (e.g., arising from foreign prosecution or litigation), harming quality; avoid creating incentives to delay submitting significant prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid discouraging meritorious appeals via high appeal fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Caution against substantial increases to notice of appeal and forwarding fees which could discourage appeals that are often invoked out of necessity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistics suggest appeals are frequently meritorious; fee increases should not be targeted to deter legitimate use of the appeal process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate PTAB funding and balanced procedural rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Fund the PTAB adequately to maintain a robust and timely process; support substantive rule changes that balance petitioners and patent owners (e.g., allowing patent owner expert declarations in preliminary responses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB received many petitions; adequate resources and sensible rulemaking preserve PTAB credibility and effectiveness; continue outreach and vigilance in decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider fee distribution models for post-grant proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Refine how PTAB fees are allocated across the process (e.g., higher percentage post-institution, pay-as-you-go, refunds if cases settle), and consider scaled petition fees for small entities based on revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More granular fee allocation could better match actual PTAB workload; scaled fees could reduce burden on individuals/small entities while ensuring PTAB funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate fee-setting approaches (front-end vs mid-prosecution vs across-the-board)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider alternatives to targeted mid-prosecution fee increases (RCE, IDS, appeals) such as raising fees across the board or increasing front-end filing/search/examination fees to distribute costs more fairly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Front-loading fees may conflict with policy to minimize entry costs, but may reduce unpredictability in prosecution costs and avoid penalizing events often outside applicant control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reevaluate maintenance fee structure and stage distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider altering maintenance fee stages (e.g., raising first/second stage fees or second stage only) because third-stage fees are high and the value profile of patents varies by technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintenance fee distribution hasn't changed despite shifting technology value profiles; adjusting stage fees could increase revenue while addressing controversies over high later-stage fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human capital: hiring, retention, training, and capacity initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase examination capacity and quality through examiner hiring/retention, targeted overtime/backlog management, nationwide workforce distribution, IT systems, and new/ongoing training programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uncertainty vs stability in budgets affects hiring; the USPTO should prioritize examiner training and capacity building to support quality and pendency goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use data-driven approaches to determine optimal pendency and reduce backlog
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure pendency, track unexamined application inventory, and implement pendency initiatives (pre-appeal, appeal conferences, RCE management, prioritized tracks) to determine and achieve optimal pendency levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiatives include improving communications, RCE inventory management, quick-path IDS, pre-appeal brief conference pilots, after-final consideration pilots, Post-Prosecution pilots, and Track One prioritized examination.
